runtime_requirements: Node.js 22.18-22.x or 23.6+, Bun 1.1.5+ or Deno 2.0+ to run the TypeScript launcher; no build step.

Java and TLA+ tools: TLA2TOOLS (path to tla2tools.jar) and optional JAVA take priority; otherwise the first run installs java@temurin-25 and tla2tools v1.7.4 (sha256 936a2620...) with mise over the network. Install tools only within task authority.
Optional SVG rendering installs the npm package pele@1.9.0 outside the repository (references/render.md).
selection: Selected at cursor/plugins main 1ba91fc (pstack 0.15.36). The author announced the skill as stable on 2026-10-29 (https://x.com/poteto/status/2115880102601101414); the repository itself carries no stability label. Community validation is provisional; see docs/decisions/statechart.md.
validation: On 2026-10-30 under macOS with Node.js 24.19 and OpenJDK 17 with tla2tools v1.7.4 (sha256 matched): every vendored file equals the upstream blob, and tests/test_statechart_vendored.py checks the digests, the recorded pin and the executable launcher; its TLC case (skipped locally without TLA2TOOLS; CI installs Java 17, Node.js 24 and the pinned jar and fails if they are missing) reported a 3-step shortest violation with exit 1 and a holding rule with exit 0. The account transaction model at reduced bounds drew an 11-state chart with every rule holding, and its no-rolling-back-mark variant reported a NoSpuriousRefusal path. The upstream test suite was not run locally; upstream #982 reports 367 passing with TLC 1.7.4. The same TLC case runs on Linux in CI. Not exercised: Bun, Deno, mise installation, Pele rendering, Windows, model-driven authoring.
packaging_notes: Vendors the runtime payload only (31 upstream files plus pstack/LICENSE). The upstream scripts/test directory (376 files, about 3.6 MB of corpus fixtures and tests that need fast-check) is not vendored; run it from a pinned upstream checkout when updating.
Keeps upstream disable-model-invocation: true, so the skill runs on explicit request or when another skill tells the agent to read it.
The --view module is user-written JavaScript or TypeScript that the command imports and runs with normal process permissions.
